Item: Should the tower be built in one piece?
Prompt / specification: The finished diagonal and turning path can exceed the room even when the tower fits upright. Options: Split at a designed fixed-shelf or connector plane | Assemble the tall case inside the closet | Build full height and hope it tips up

Item: How will hanging and shelf zones be allocated?
Prompt / specification: Clothing dimensions, rod height, shelf thickness, and drawer fronts compete for the same vertical space. Options: Lay out from measured wardrobe categories | Use adjustable zones within a fixed structural frame | Divide the tower into equal boxes

Item: Where will room variation be absorbed?
Prompt / specification: Closet walls and floors are rarely square enough for a full-width rigid assembly. Options: Use level base plus side and top fit parts | Leave a deliberate open reveal at one side | Wedge the tower between both walls

Project value / evidence: Evidence: Closet elevation plus wardrobe and delivery-path records. Hold: Stop if ceiling low point, doorway clearance, or wall structure is unverified.

Prompt / specification: Convert storage demand into modular zones, hardware clearances, fit parts, and installation sequence.
Project value / evidence: Evidence: Released elevation, module sections, and hardware schedule. Hold: Stop if a drawer, rod, or module cannot be assembled and serviced in sequence.

Prompt / specification: Produce paired sides, aligned shelf-pin rows, square modules, and clearly separated fit parts.
Project value / evidence: Evidence: Labeled modules with matching pin patterns and passing hardware sample. Hold: Stop if handed panels or module break references become ambiguous.

Prompt / specification: Build square transportable modules and prove drawers, shelves, and rods before entering the closet.
Project value / evidence: Evidence: Square modules with recorded diagonals and complete dry-stack height. Hold: Stop if stacked joints depend on wall pressure or hidden inaccessible fasteners.

Prompt / specification: Level, stack, connect, anchor, and fit the system without losing door or drawer clearance.
Project value / evidence: Evidence: Anchored system with level, restraint, filler, and movement-clearance evidence. Hold: Stop if a module cannot be restrained before the next one is lifted into place.

Prompt / specification: Load representative contents, test moving components, and record adjustment and capacity limits.
Project value / evidence: Evidence: Loaded function test and final closet configuration record. Hold: Do not close while a tower moves, a drawer rubs, or a rod support loosens.

Prompt / specification: Use when the standing tower fits but its tip-up diagonal or doorway turn does not.
Project value / evidence: A designed horizontal joint, connector access, and stacking restraint divide the case into transportable modules.

Prompt / specification: Use when measured garments leave enough vertical space for drawers and two independent rod zones.
Project value / evidence: Drawer fronts, rod sockets, shelf thickness, and clothing drop must share one reconciled elevation.

Prompt / specification: Use where wall work is limited but an allowed anti-tip method and deliberate side reveals are available.
Project value / evidence: Removable fillers handle room variation while the tower still needs positive restraint and clean disassembly.

Prompt / specification: The delivery mockup or diagonal calculation touches ceiling, door head, corner, or closet opening.
Project value / evidence: Hold fabrication, introduce a designed module break, and rerun the route with the largest finished module.

Prompt / specification: Shelf pins form mismatched elevations or front/rear offsets across paired tower sides.
Project value / evidence: Quarantine the pair, confirm face and bottom datums, and recut or repair only through a verified symmetric jig plan.

Prompt / specification: Drawer travel, shelf seating, or diagonals change when the tower meets baseboard or floor variation.
Project value / evidence: Release restraint, level the base and fit external trim, restore case square, then re-anchor.

Prompt / specification: Hanging garments, rod socket screws, or rod support enters drawer travel or usable opening.
Project value / evidence: Stop hardware installation and reconcile the complete vertical and depth sections before drilling more parts.

Prompt / specification: The closet tower reaches the room in proven modules, stands square on its own leveled base, and serves the measured wardrobe without hardware collisions.
Every finished module travels through the recorded route and connects without forcing walls, ceiling, or case joints.
The installed tower remains level and plumb with positive restraint at the documented structure.
Drawers complete full loaded travel, shelves sit at matching pin elevations, and rods remain secure under representative clothing.
Long-hang, double-hang, folded, shoe, and drawer zones retain the clear dimensions promised in the wardrobe brief.
